newsitem.title: USA: Oregon approves Enron, Portland merger.
newsitem.headline: Oregon approves Enron, Portland merger.

text.p: Oregon Public Utility Commission gave final endorsement Wednesday to the planned $2.1 billion merger of Enron Corp and Portland General Corp, parent of Portland General Electric Co.
"Our main concern throughout the process was the impact the merger would have on customers," said Commission Chairman Roger Hamilton in a statement.

The vote ends a contentious approval process at the state regulatory agency, where staff initially recommended denial of the deal on the grounds it did not guarantee any benefits to customers of the Oregon electric utility.

But Houston-based Enron in mid-April gave up its hard-line tactics and agreed to grant $141 million in customer rate reductions and to meet other negotiated conditions in return for approval of the deal.
To pay for the rate cuts, the companies lowered the share exchange ratio of the deal to 0.9825 shares of Enron stock for every share of Portland General stock from the previous one-for-one ratio.
As a result of the rate-cut commitment, the OPUC staff in late April issued a formal recommendation to the three-member commission to approve the deal. More
"Our goal was to make sure that consumers are better off because of the merger than if it didn't happen," Hamilton said.

Kenneth Lay, Enron's chairman, said in a statement the "new combined company will be strategically positioned to be a leader in the exciting changes taking place in the rapidly deregulating and competitive electricity and gas industries."

He noted the company, which also agreed to allow competition within Portland General's service territory, will be working closely with the OPUC over the next three months to develop a detailed customer choice filing for Oregon.
Portland General shareholders are scheduled to vote on the revised merger agreement June 24.
